children: Shares of MTAR Technologies hit the 5 percent upper circuit limit in Monday's trade as its key client Bloom Energy is set to join the S&P 500 index.
The stock was trading at Rs 7,519 per share on the NSE.
The sharp rise in the stock came amid reports that Bloom Energy will join the S&P 500 in the upcoming quarterly rebalancing, replacing Molson Coors Beverage.
The index inclusion is expected to draw interest from institutional investors and passive funds tracking the S&P 500.
Bloom Energy's inclusion reflects its market capitalisation and eligibility under the index provider's criteria.

MTAR Technologies' association with Bloom Energy, which supplies fuel cell solutions for AI data centres, has strengthened its positioning in the segment. Bloom Energy's fuel cells are expected to be deployed in a proposed 1.8 GW data centre project in Cheyenne, Wyoming.

Bloom Energy designs, manufactures, sells and installs solid oxide fuel cell systems that provide on-site power generation for customers in the US and internationally. The company has a market capitalisation of USD 69.4 billion and operates in the electrical industry segment.
